facts: The paper 'Emigration and radical right populism' was authored by Rafaela Dancygier, Sirus H. Dehdari, David D. Laitin, Moritz Marbach, and Kåre Vernby.
The paper was published on 2024-03-27 in the American Journal of Political Science (DOI: 10.1111/ajps.12852).
The study examines how internal and international emigration of citizens influences populist radical right (PRR) electoral success.
The authors identify two complementary mechanisms: emigration alters the composition of the electorate and changes the preferences of those left behind.
Across Europe at the subnational level, the study establishes a positive correlation between PRR vote shares and net-migration loss.
A fine-grained panel analysis of precincts in Sweden shows citizen departures increase PRR vote shares in places of emigration.
The Swedish panel analysis shows that the Social Democrats are the principal losers from citizen emigration.
Elite interviews and newspaper analyses show emigration generates material and psychological grievances that populists exploit and established parties fail to address effectively.
